newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen signs pact with former Cambodian premier.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen signs pact with former Cambodian premier.

text.p: The Cambodian People's Party (CPP) on Tuesday signed an alliance with the party of former prime minister and one-time royalist In Tam.
Co-Premier Hun Sen signed a cooperation accord with the Democratic Party's deputy leader Ouk Phure, in the absence of the ailing 79-year-old In Tam.

The agreement was the latest in a series of alliances signed by the CPP with smaller parties since its royalist rival in the coalition government, the FUNCINPEC party, said in January it would form a front of parties ahead of 1998 general elections.
In Tam served as interior minister and agriculture minister during the 1960s and served as prime minister in 1973.

He was a founding member and top official of King Norodom Sihanouk's FUNCINPEC party, which was set up in 1981 to fight the Phnom Penh government set up by Vietnam after it ousted the brutal Khmer Rouge regime in 1979.
In Tam later left to live in the United States but returned to lead his Democratic Party in U.N.-run general elections in 1993. The party failed to win a seat.

FUNCINPEC and the CPP set up an uneasy coalition government after those elections, but ties have worsened in the past year due to rows over power-sharing and how to handle the defection of thousands of Khmer Rouge troops.
